senses.gloss:
Nalada, ‘nard’ (Nardastachys Jatamansi) is a plant mentioned
in the Atharvaveda,^1 in the Aitareya^2 and the Śāṅkhāyana^3
Āraṇyakas (where it is mentioned as used for a garland), as well as
in the Sūtras. In the Atharvaveda^4 the feminine form of the word,
Naladī, occurs as the name of an Apsaras, or celestial nymph.
1) vi. 102, 3.
2) iii. 2, 4.
3) xi. 4.
4) iv. 37, 3.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 68,
69; Grohmann, Indische Studien, 9, 420;
Caland, Altindisches Zauberritual, 177,
n. 4.
